pNone_chapter_1: In a sun-drenched living room in a traditional Bengali house, Byomkesh Bakshi sits in a wooden armchair, leaning forward with a silver cigarette case held open towards an unseen guest. He wears a crisp white dhoti and kurta, his sharp eyes focused with quiet intensity, while Ajit stands nearby near a large open window that overlooks the lush greenery of Hindustan Park. The warm afternoon light filters through the slats of the shutters, casting long, geometric shadows across the polished floorboards and the simple wooden furniture. A ceiling fan rotates slowly above, and the atmosphere is thick with the golden haze of a quiet Sunday.
